records.purchase_evidence_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
records.purchase_instructions: Before beginning the process to purchase an adjudicated property with our office, you must first determine that the property in which you are interested has in fact been adjudicated, and is still adjudicated, to the City-Parish. You will need to research the property you are interested in with the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff, the East Baton Rouge Parish Clerk of Court, and the East Baton Rouge Parish Assessor. Once you have determined that the property in which you are interested is adjudicated, you must call the Parish Attorney's Office so that someone in our office can confirm that the property is still currently available. Opening a "file" with our office to purchase adjudicated property will require the following: A completed "Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property" form; the legal description and property ID number if known; the name of the owner in whose name the property was sold (adjudicated) and the year of the tax sale; a certified check or money order for advanced costs for each piece of property you open a file on. After you have submitted all of the required documents and costs, and our office has confirmed the availability of the property, an appraisal will be ordered for the property. You will also be asked to make an initial "offer" (purchase price) both verbally and in writing. Once an offer is received, this office will introduce an ordinance to the Metropolitan Council requesting the property be sold at public auction. You will be notified of the date and time to appear for the public bidding.

acquisition.office: Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division, City of Baton Rouge / Parish of East Baton Rouge
acquisition.mailing_address: Parish Attorney's Office, Property Section, P.O. Box 1471, Baton Rouge, LA 70821
acquisition.payment: Certified check or money order for the advanced costs, per parcel; no personal checks or cash (advanced costs are not part of the purchase price)
steps: Confirm the property is still adjudicated with the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff, Clerk of Court and Assessor (properties are redeemed during the year)
Call the Parish Attorney's Office to confirm the property is still currently available

Open a file: the Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property form, the legal description / property ID, the owner and year of the tax sale (from the Sheriff), and a certified check or money order for the advanced costs
An appraisal is ordered; make an initial offer verbally and in writing
The office introduces an ordinance to the Metropolitan Council for a public auction; appear at the public bidding on the date you are notified of

records.purchase_evidence_title: Galveston County Sheriff's Office - Sheriff Sales Information & Procedures
records.purchase_instructions: TAX FORECLOSURE SALES/RESALES Tax foreclosure sales/resales are conducted by the Galveston County Sheriff exclusively through an online platform and website operated by Real Auction. There will be no live auctions of tax foreclosures and/or resales. Bidder Registration - Bidders must register through the Real Auction website. Bid Deposits - After registering through the Real Auction website, bidders must deposit with the Galveston County Sheriff an amount equal to at least five percent (5%) of the total amount of their bids. Winning bid amounts can be delivered by wire transfer through the Real Auction website, or by money order or cashier's check to the Galveston County Sheriff's Office by 4:00 PM on the day of the sale. If you are the winning bidder, you must furnish the Galveston County Sheriff's Office with a Certificate of Eligibility in order for the Sheriff's Deed to be recorded in the county deed records.
